shared_elements: monumental upright stone monolith carved in low relief
anthropomorphic body schema (head/upper zone, torso, lower garment)
circle or disc motif on the chest/torso
horizontal band or belt encircling the body
arms/limbs rendered in shallow relief against the block
repeated small rectangular/loop motifs in a row along an upper band
broad plain lower zone read as a skirt or loincloth
justification: Both are large anthropomorphic stone monoliths organised into the same vertical scheme: a headed upper zone, a row of small repeated motifs, arms in shallow relief flanking a prominent disc on the torso, a horizontal belt-like band, and a plain skirt below — a fairly specific shared compositional logic. They differ sharply in execution and mass: A is a thin, flat-faced slab with crisp, linear, almost graphic carving including clearly identifiable animals in profile, while B is a bulky, rounded, three-dimensional block whose motifs are soft, eroded and largely non-figural.
